name: Lobkowicz Palace
architectural_style: Renaissance palace; constructed 1570–1576; substantially rebuilt in Baroque style between 1651 and 1668 by architect Giovanni Domenico Orsi; the interior retains elaborate Baroque ceiling frescoes, period state rooms, and the private Lobkowicz family art collection; the palace is the only private property within the Prague Castle complex

opening_hours.seasonal_note: The Lobkowicz Palace museum is open daily 10:00–18:00 (last entry 17:30). The midday classical concert series runs Tuesday through Sunday at 13:00 (check lobkowicz.cz for current schedule and dates — some dates are skipped for private events). The palace is inside the Prague Castle complex, which has its own entry hours; approach via the castle gates.

best_season: Year-round — the palace is open daily and concerts run throughout the year; spring and autumn avoid peak summer queues for the wider Prague Castle complex
accessibility: The palace is largely accessible on the ground and first floor levels via a lift. The audio guide is included with museum admission. Concert venue (palace music room) is accessible.
tagline: The only privately owned palace in Prague Castle — housing Bruegel, Canaletto, and Beethoven's Eroica manuscript, with a renowned midday concert series in the palace's original music rooms
highlights: The Lobkowicz family art collection — Pieter Bruegel the Elder's Haymaking (1565), Canaletto's views of London, and works by Velázquez, Lucas Cranach, and Jan Brueghel the Elder

Beethoven's Eroica Symphony manuscript — the original hand-corrected score with Beethoven's own revisions, including the famous deletion of Napoleon's dedication; one of the most important musical manuscripts in the world
Mozart's Don Giovanni — an original manuscript copy annotated in Mozart's own hand, acquired by the Lobkowicz family during Mozart's Prague period
Midday classical concerts in the palace's original music rooms — a 1-hour performance by resident musicians in the room where Beethoven and Mozart themselves performed
The only private property inside the Prague Castle complex — returned to the Lobkowicz family in 2002 after 55 years of communist-era confiscation
description:
Lobkowicz Palace is the most exceptional private house museum in the Czech Republic — and one of the finest in central Europe. Situated at the eastern end of the Prague Castle complex, it is the only palace within the castle that is privately owned: returned to the Lobkowicz family in 2002 after confiscation by the Nazi occupation (1939) and subsequent communist nationalisation (1948), its collections were reunited and the palace opened as a museum and concert venue the same year.

The palace's art collection was assembled by the Lobkowicz family over four centuries and is extraordinary by any measure. Pieter Bruegel the Elder's Haymaking (1565) — one of his famous cycle of Months paintings, only three of which remain in private hands — is the centrepiece. Canaletto's panoramic views of the Thames at Richmond and the city of London are among the finest of his English works. The collection also includes Velázquez, Lucas Cranach the Elder, Jan Brueghel, and an extensive armoury.

The musical manuscripts are perhaps even more significant. Beethoven's Eroica Symphony: the original working score, with the famous crossed-out dedication to Napoleon (Beethoven's rage at Napoleon's coronation as Emperor in 1804 led him to erase the title 'Bonaparte' so violently that the manuscript is torn at that point). The Lobkowicz family were Beethoven's principal patrons in Vienna — Prince Joseph Franz Maximilian Lobkowicz gave Beethoven an annual stipend and was the dedicatee of the Eroica, Symphonies 5 and 6, and the string quartets. Mozart's Don Giovanni connection: the manuscript copy in the Lobkowicz collection is annotated in Mozart's own hand from his 1787 Prague period, when Don Giovanni premiered at the Estates Theatre.
history:
The Lobkowicz family — Bohemian nobility of the highest rank, later elevated to the Imperial title of Prince — were among the most powerful magnates in the Habsburg Monarchy for three centuries. Their support of the Habsburgs during the Thirty Years' War (and specifically their alignment with the Catholic side against the Protestant Bohemian nobility after the Battle of White Mountain in 1620) brought them enormous landholdings confiscated from Protestant families.

The palace at Prague Castle was acquired in 1651 and rebuilt in Baroque style between 1651 and 1668. Through the 18th century the family developed into major cultural patrons: Prince Joseph Franz Maximilian Lobkowicz (1772–1816) was arguably the most important single patron of Beethoven's career, supporting him financially through a formal annuity and premiering several of the major symphonies at Lobkowicz family palaces in Vienna and Prague.

The confiscations came in two waves. The Nazi occupation of Czechoslovakia (1939) seized the family's Bohemian properties. The communist nationalisation of 1948 completed the transfer of everything remaining, including the palace and its collections. William Lobkowicz — an American citizen who had grown up outside Czechoslovakia — began the restitution process after 1989 and succeeded in recovering the palace, its collections, and other family properties under Czechoslovak and Czech restitution legislation. The Lobkowicz family reopened the palace in 2007 as a privately operated museum and concert venue.
how_to_visit:
**Getting there:** The palace is at the eastern end of Prague Castle, a 5-minute walk through the complex from the main entrance on Hradčanské náměstí. Take tram 22, 23, or 41 to Pražský hrad or Pohořelec; alternatively, tram to Malostranské náměstí and walk up Nerudova street.

**Tickets:** Walk-up museum entry is 350 CZK adult, 180 CZK child, available at the palace entrance on Jiřská street; the audio guide narrated by Lobkowicz family members is included. The GYG midday concert ticket (t48430, from €25, 4.6★/1,209 reviews) includes both the 1-hour concert and museum entry — concerts run at 13:00 Tuesday through Sunday and some dates sell out; book in advance.

**Practical tips:** Lobkowicz Palace is not included in any standard Prague Castle circuit ticket (A, B, or C) — a separate ticket is always required. The family-narrated audio guide is one of the better audio guides in Prague and is worth following from the first room.

**Combine with:** [Prague Castle](/castles/czech-republic/prague-castle) — the surrounding state-managed complex with St Vitus Cathedral and the Royal Palace, immediately adjacent on the same hill.

faqs.question: Is Lobkowicz Palace included in the Prague Castle ticket?
faqs.answer: No — Lobkowicz Palace is privately owned and operated separately from the state-managed Prague Castle complex. The standard Prague Castle combined tickets (circuits A, B, and C) do not include Lobkowicz Palace. A separate ticket (CZK 350 adult) is required for the museum, or the concert ticket (€25 via GYG) which includes both the midday concert and museum entry. The palace is inside the castle complex but accessible only with its own ticket.

faqs.question: What is the story behind Beethoven's Eroica manuscript here?
faqs.answer: Beethoven composed the Eroica Symphony (Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major) between 1803 and 1804, originally intending to dedicate it to Napoleon Bonaparte — whom Beethoven admired as a figure of Enlightenment values. When Napoleon crowned himself Emperor in December 1804, Beethoven was enraged: his pupil Ferdinand Ries recorded that Beethoven grabbed the title page of the manuscript, tore it, and crossed out Napoleon's name so violently that the paper was damaged. The working manuscript in the Lobkowicz collection — one of several copies from the composition process — shows this correction. The symphony was re-dedicated to Prince Lobkowicz himself, who premiered it at his Vienna palace in 1804.

faqs.question: Can I book the midday concert separately from the museum?
faqs.answer: The midday concert ticket (€25 via GYG, t48430) includes museum entry as part of the package — you cannot book just the concert without the museum component. For visitors who only want to see the museum, the standalone museum ticket (CZK 350) is available at the palace entrance without advance booking. The GYG concert ticket is the better value option if you plan to see both.
